chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Stuff Smith sold him a record machine; the rattlesnake in the Alphonso Trent car
summary: Years earlier in Washington Stuff conned him into buying a disc recorder, and told of a snake thrown into the Trent band's car in Texas.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Uh, trying to think, oh, gosh. I -- because I know -- I knew Stuff -- I'm trying to figure -- because I met Stuffy years ago, in Washington, D. C., when I was living in Washington, I was working at the Howard Theater. 'Cause he sold me a recording, a -- an apparatus there, machine.
Disk recorder, it must have been back then.
Yeah, yeah, one of them things, and some records, and things. And it was a snow job. He laughs like hell about it. He --
(Laughter.)
I say you're rotten. You're dirty. He says, what's the matter, man?! Blah, blah, blah, blah, he used to tell me about the times he was with Trent, Alphonso Trent.
Alphonso Trent.
Trent in Texas, and he told me some stories about that that were terrific.
What, he was doing a con job?
Yeah, he was -- he was -- no, he was in there, and this wasn't when I was with the carnival.
Yes, I mean you were talking about the stories with Alphonso Trent, but they --
Yeah, but this very one in particular,

they said they were doing one nighters, going from here to there, and sitting in the car, and they'd be working at night, and they were riding along, going through the desert somewhere in Texas, and they ran over a rattlesnake, or a snake, or some kind of snake, and as the wheels turned, somehow, the snake came around and they brought him up, or threw him in the car. (Laughs.)

And all the guys was laying there asleep, snoring, you know, trying to wake up, and day was just breaking, slightly (laughs) had some guy feel this thing moving in his lap, and he reached down there and he said aaaah! He grabbed the thing and handed it to Stuff. He said Aaah! what is this? And threw it out the car, you know.
(Laughter.)
The same snake that they ran over, you know. They got -- but nobody got bitten by the damned thing, but everybody was excited and going nuts.
The snake must have been in bad shape.
Yeah, and so was the man.
(Laughter.)

And things like that, so he came to my house and I had -- I needed a record player, and he talked me into it, and he said man, this and that, so I said okay, I think I give him five or six dollars for it. And some
records, and I didn't see Stuff no more, and the next time I saw him I had to catch him. I said man, that was nothing. He laughed! He knew. You know.
(Laughter.)
That wasn't why he gave you a job, though, was it?
No, no, no. No. I'm trying to think, this -- had we worked together, or where? Had we worked together, why did he give me this job?
